messages.content: Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

output:
Draft below (245 words), written against the human-prose checklist and clean through the project's own `slopwatch` gate. Prices and the support address are placeholders — swap in real numbers.

---

# Pricing

Every plan reviews your pull requests line by line. The difference is how much history the reviewer gets to see, and who you can call when it's wrong.

## Solo — $0

For one person and one repo. Unlimited reviews on public repos, 200 private-repo reviews a month. Comments land on the PR within 90 seconds of the push. No card.

Good enough that a lot of people never leave it. That's fine.

## Team — $19 per developer per month

Everything in Solo, plus the part that matters: the reviewer reads your whole repo, not just the diff. It learns that your codebase already has a retry helper before it suggests you write a third one.

You also get review rules written in plain English ("never call the payments client outside `billing/`"), a dashboard showing which findings your team actually accepted, and SSO through Google or Okta. Fourteen-day trial, no card.

## Enterprise — talk to us

Self-hosted or in your own VPC, so no source code crosses your network edge. SAML, SCIM, audit logs, and a signed agreement that your code is never used to train anything.

Add a named engineer who tunes the rules against your last six months of merged PRs, and a 4-hour support response, business hours in your timezone.

---

Annual billing takes 20% off Team. Nonprofits and students get Team free — email us from your .edu address.

Questions about a plan? support@example.com. A person answers.

---

Two choices worth a second look: the free tier is framed as genuinely sufficient rather than crippled (builds trust, costs you the users who'd never convert anyway), and each tier leads with one concrete mechanism instead of a feature list. If you want a harder upsell on Team, say the word.
